close_reason: Won't fix: opinion-tagged. RFC 8620 §5.2 mandates these fields are present (even when empty), so strict deserialization correctly catches non-conformant servers. Adding #[serde(default)] would silently mask server bugs that should surface as errors. Reopen if a real-world server is observed omitting the fields and we need to interop with it.
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:52-60 ChangesResponse has `created: Vec<Id>`, `updated: Vec<Id>`, `destroyed: Vec<Id>` (no Option, no #[serde(default)]).

RFC 8620 §5.2 says these fields are required and present even when empty. So the current shape is correct — but it relies on the server obeying the spec. A buggy server that omits e.g. `destroyed` when nothing was destroyed will fail deserialization with 'missing field destroyed.'

A defensive choice: `#[serde(default)] pub destroyed: Vec<Id>` — spec-compliant servers send the empty array (no change), broken servers that omit get an empty Vec instead of a runtime error. Costs nothing.

This is the inverse of finding .27 — there, the over-Option-ed fields propagate uncertainty; here, the under-Option-ed fields refuse to forgive minor server bugs. The defaultable choice gives both: optional-on-the-wire, present-in-the-type.
title: ChangesResponse fields like created/updated/destroyed not Option — but spec says they may be empty arrays
